about: Data of Learn case file CF5, Where should a cogeneration study's boundary be drawn? The timeline and the boundary card are approved excerpt wording (E14), word for word (E14.22, E14.21); the boundary card's source line is E14.24. The idea is the course's own toy: a generic steam plant and one generic load with round numbers the reader sets, average power over one hour; nothing in it is the study's input, equation or result.

timeline.title: The study in time
timeline.lede: One dated step: the accepted paper.

events.label: Paper accepted
events.text: An hourly model prices the steam sent to cooling by the turbine work it gives up, and compares the plant, with and without steam cooling, with grid supply and an on-site gas combined cycle.

source.label: Li et al. (2026), accepted paper, Energy Conversion and Management; DOI pending

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: steam sent to cooling is steam the low-pressure turbine does not convert, so it costs the turbine work it gives up;
ERCOT's hourly prices for the market years 2022 to 2024;
hourly average, not marginal, emission factors;
the plant is one fixed unit;
steam is taken at the turbine crossover, and a sweep of the penalty tests that choice.
leaves: reliability on a common basis across options;
boundary.source: From: Li et al. (2026), accepted paper, Energy Conversion and Management; DOI pending.

idea.title: One hour at a steam plant beside a large load
idea.note: Illustrative round numbers you set: a generic steam plant and one load that needs power and cooling, not the study's inputs or results. Average power during one hour, in MW; auxiliary electricity for pumps and fans is left out.
